raw_response:
I have farmed these 14 mu for fifty years. Last year was alright, so I will not change much. My neighbors all do about the same.

For wheat, I plant in October after I rotary till the maize stubble. I use the improved Jimai seed the dealer sells — everyone here uses it, about 15 kg per mu. For base fertilizer I put down 2 bags of diammonium (DAP, 50 kg bag) every mu before sowing, then one bag of urea (50 kg) topdressing at spring green-up. That comes out to about 25 kg nitrogen per mu. I add a half bag of potash too because the soil here is getting tired. I water four times — the winter water, green-up, jointing, and grain-filling — I have the well so it is only the electricity cost. Spray twice for weeds and aphids. I expect around 480 kg per mu, same as last year.

For maize, I direct-seed right after the wheat combine, no tillage, hybrid seed from the same dealer. One bag of compound 15-15-15 at planting, then a bag of urea at the big flare stage — about 22 kg nitrogen per mu. Summer rains give me most of the water but I run the well once or twice if July is dry. One spray for borers and weeds is enough. I get 550 kg per mu usually.

I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than lose the harvest. Losing yield costs much more than one bag.
